requirements: 0–4 years (T1: 0–2; T2: 1–4) — and zero is a real number here. If you’ve owned product outcomes end-to-end, show us. If you haven’t held the title yet, show us the closest thing you have owned end-to-end: a research project, a product you designed, an analysis someone acted on.

You design — and this is the one that doesn’t flex. You can produce flows and screens complete enough that an engineer builds from them without interpreting. We look at the design itself: not the file format, and not where you learned it. We’re firm here because the design handoff is the part of our process that already works, and we’re not willing to regress it.
You settle edge cases before handoff, not during implementation. If a flow has four failure states, all four are in the spec.
Direct with management. You can take a decision into a room with senior stakeholders, defend it with evidence, and change your mind in public when the evidence says so.
You talk to users yourself — and you do it without being asked to.
Builder mode — a hard bar here, not a bonus. The “/ Builder” in the title is the job:

You prototype your own ideas with AI tools (Claude Code, Claude Design, Figma Make, or equivalent). The bar is a clickable demo in a day, to make an idea concrete before engineering invests in it — not production-grade.
You self-serve your own data questions — funnel, retention, cohort — without queueing a request. Natural-language-to-SQL counts; hand-writing joins is not the bar.
You write a 10-row eval set for any AI feature you touch: concrete examples of what good output looks like.
And you review what AI produces rather than passing it on. That review is the part we’re hiring for.
Proficient in Cantonese, Mandarin, and English — our users, suppliers, and team move across all three.
Nice to have:

A design background — or a data, CS, information-systems, or analytical one. All of them feed this role well, and none is required. They tend to arrive with opposite halves: design backgrounds bring craft and flow thinking; data, CS and analytical backgrounds bring the instinct that a claim might be wrong — which is most of the “verified” bar above — and usually a head start on the builder bar. Expect us to press you hardest on the half you didn’t arrive with — bring evidence for both.
Shipping small changes yourself via PR — copy, a config value, a flag — with a reviewer. Above the bar, not at it.
Experience somewhere the design and the product decision already sat with the same person.
Growth product work, or comfort being measured partly on metrics moved.
Working with engineering teams of 3–8
The Opportunity for Talent:

Best fit for someone who would rather decide than escalate, who treats an unanswered question in their own spec as a defect, and who wants the design call and the product call to be the same job rather than two.
Buy&Ship is Hong Kong’s leading cross-border shipping platform. Hong Kong shoppers source from Japan, Korea, the US and beyond, and we’re the bridge that makes those purchases land at their door.

This role is unusual in one specific way: you own the product decision and the design, together. Not a PM who briefs a designer, and not a designer who executes someone else’s spec — one person who decides what we build, decides what it looks like, and hands engineering something complete enough to build from without coming back.

The “/ Builder” is literal, and it’s bounded. You prototype to discover — a demo that makes an idea concrete enough to put in front of someone. Production and scaling stay with engineers. You’re not hired to write the shipped code; you’re hired so that fewer wrong things get built.

We work this way because the limit on how fast we ship is no longer how fast code gets written. It’s whether the decisions upstream of the code were actually settled. When they aren’t, engineering stops and comes back — and every one of those round trips costs more than making the decision properly the first time would have.
The role is open at T1 (Associate PM, 0–2 yrs) or T2 (PM, 1–4 yrs). Apply once; we’ll set the level to your experience and capability.

If you’re graduating, or coming from data or design rather than product management — apply. We’re hiring for a profile that is genuinely new: product judgment, design, and real AI fluency in one person. The people who have that combination often haven’t held a PM title yet, and we’d rather find them than wait. What we test is whether you can do the work.

Company Introduction

As a bank consortium, JETCO currently has more than 30 member banks and connects around 3,000 ATMs in Hong Kong and Macau to provide convenient and reliable ATM services across both locations. JETCO ATM switching network also connects to multiple international ATM networks.

JETCO also offers a series of value-added services to member banks, such as payment gateway for e-Commerce and inter-bank cardless cash withdrawal service, to enable member banks to provide customers with innovative and high-quality services.

In 2018, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority designated the relevant payment systems operated by JETCO for the processing of Hong Kong retail payment transactions as a designated retail payment system (“designated RPS”) pursuant to the Payment Systems and Stored Value Facilities Ordinance (“PSSVFO”).

In 2019, JETCO launched JETCO APIX, the first open API exchange platform in Hong Kong. By riding on JETCO APIX, banks and other institution customers can interconnect with their business partners in various industries via API to co-develop innovative products and services for improving service quality and customer experience.

In 2022, JETCO CDI Portal for data consumers launched for supporting banks to easily onboard to Commercial Data Interchange (“CDI”), and JETCO has been named as a solution provider of CDI. In 2023, JETCO CDI Portal has extended to support data providers to onboard to CDI. Moreover, JETCO CDI APIs & value-added features for data consumers were launched. Coming will have more value-added features launching for both data consumers and data providers.

In July 2024, JETCO IADS Proxy Service launched for supporting banks to participate HKMA’s Interbank Account Data Sharing (“IADS”) programme as the data consuming bank to retrieve their customers’ bank account data from other banks subject to customer consents.

In October 2024, JETCO has joined as the participant in Project Ensemble and has connected to Ensemble Sandbox, as well as completed PoC by partnering with banks to testify Payment-versus-Payment (“PvP”) and Delivery-versus-Payment (“DvP”) scenarios. In November 2025, we become one of the participants of EnsembleTX and partnered with banks to test different use cases of interbank settlement using tokenised deposit (“TD”) by riding on our distributed ledger technology (“DLT”) TD platform.

o Architectural Designer: Drive the architectural elements, structural coordination, and statutory compliance of the technical drawings.
o Assistant Design Project Manager: Independently manage project timelines, daily contractor coordination, and assist with tender process and budget tracking.

Cell Culture: Culture, expand, and maintain a range of mammalian and other cell lines and primary cells relevant to our application programs — including primary pancreatic islet cells, iPSC-derived cells, immune cells, mesenchymal stem cells, CHO, or others, as well as microbial culture of bacteria, yeast, or algae — with rigorous attention to viability, sterility, and mycoplasma testing.

Hydrogel Formulation & Optimisation: Design, formulate, and optimise hydrogel systems (e.g., alginate, PEG-based, or other biocompatible polymers) specifically for cell encapsulation, tuning gelation chemistry, mechanical properties, permeability, and biocompatibility to the requirements of each cell type and application.

Microfluidic Encapsulation Integration: Work closely with microfluidics and optical engineering teams to adapt hydrogel-cell formulations for droplet generation on the RAINSort platform, troubleshooting issues such as viscosity mismatches, clogging, gelation kinetics, and capsule uniformity.

Capsule Quality & Performance Characterisation: Develop and run assays to evaluate capsule quality metrics — encapsulation efficiency, empty-capsule carryover, post-encapsulation cell viability, membrane permeability, mechanical integrity, and long-term functional performance (e.g., glucose-stimulated insulin secretion for islet cell capsules).

Application-Specific Development: Support specific application programs across the Company's adjacency areas, including pancreatic islet / artificial pancreas encapsulation, iPSC-derived nephron progenitor cell encapsulation, CAR-T and Treg cell therapy encapsulation, MSC/exosome spheroid production, organoid biobanking, and other cell encapsulation projects.

Cross-functional Collaboration: Partner with the optical and software engineering teams to co-develop encapsulation protocols compatible with automated AI-driven sorting, and work with business development to translate partner and customer requirements (e.g., academic and pharma collaborators) into cell culture and formulation protocols.

Customer acquisition and support: Assist in identifying potential customers/user leads, contacting them, and acquiring customers for our products, as well as follow up support and technical advisement.

Documentation & Compliance: Maintain detailed lab notebooks, SOPs, and technical reports for cell culture and hydrogel formulation work. Support regulatory submissions (e.g., ISO 13485) and GMP-adjacent documentation with clear, traceable records.
Core Qualifications

Education: Master's degree or PhD in Cell Biology, Bioengineering, Chemistry, Biomedical Engineering, Materials Science, Biomaterials, or a closely related field. Bachelor's with exceptional previous industry experience may be considered.

Experience: 5+ years of hands-on experience in mammalian cell culture, with direct, demonstrable experience in hydrogel formulation and optimisation for cell encapsulation. Experience with microfluidic encapsulation, cell therapy manufacturing, or biomaterials-based drug/cell delivery is required.
Technical Skills
Proficiency in mammalian and other cell line culture techniques: passaging, expansion, cryopreservation, and viability assays (e.g., Trypan blue, Calcein-AM/EthD, flow cytometry-based viability).

Hands-on hydrogel/biomaterial formulation experience: alginate, PEG-based, gelatin methacrylate (GelMA), collagen, or other biocompatible polymers, with an understanding of ionic, photo-, or thermal crosslinking chemistries.
Experience characterising hydrogel properties, including rheology, swelling ratio, degradation kinetics, mechanical testing (compression/tensile), and permeability/diffusion assays.
Familiarity with microfluidic droplet generation and cell encapsulation techniques (e.g., flow-focusing, T-junction, or coaxial encapsulation).
Understanding of cell–material interactions, biocompatibility, and immune response considerations relevant to encapsulated cell therapies.
Experience with relevant analytical and characterisation tools: fluorescence/confocal microscopy, flow cytometry, and functional assays (e.g., ELISA, glucose-stimulated insulin secretion).

Instrument Integration: Demonstrated ability, or strong willingness, to work closely with optical and microfluidics engineering teams to co-develop encapsulation protocols compatible with automated cell sorting and imaging platforms.
